we have presented a new model for aggregate evacuation time on path networks with unknown number of evacuees, and we have developed an algorithm that is asymptotically faster than the previous fastest one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of locating an evacuation center on a path network to optimize the aggregate time of evacuees, where the numbers of the evacuees at each location are given by upper bounds.
a new optimization criterion and a new network model, and we present the first efficient algorithm to solve the resulting optimization problem.

the algorithm is $O(n^{\min\{3, 2 + \frac{1}{\log n}\}})$-time.
the aggregate evacuation time is minimized by a 1-sink at the midpoint of the path.
our algorithm is the fastest known algorithm for the 1-sink problem on path networks, when the number of vertices $n\ge 3$.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present the first algorithm that can compute the optimal sink location in linear time for a path network.
, we provide a new model for evacuation planning and a faster algorithm for the case of a path network and a single sink.
the aggregate evacuation time can be minimized in $O(n^5)$ time for general graphs, and in $O(n\log n)$ for path networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aggregate evacuation time is not necessarily minimized at the middle of the path, but at a location that depends on the upper and lower bounds on the number of evacuees.
the optimal sink location for minimizing maximum "regret" is not the median vertex of the path.
the optimal sink location for minimizing the aggregate evacuation time can be very far from the center of the path, depending on the distribution of the evacuees.
